title: Closed subsets proper over a base; support of a module; modules with support proper over a base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. (1) A closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ is *proper over $S$* if the composite $f\circ i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to X\to S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], where $i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme structure on $Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]: the closed subscheme of $X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of the local sections of $\mathcal O_X$ vanishing at every point of $Z$; it is the unique reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] closed subscheme of $X$ with underlying set $Z$, up to unique isomorphism over $X$, so the condition does not depend on any choice. (2) For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ (a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying space of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) its *support* is the set $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x\in X:\mathcal F_x\neq0\}$, $\mathcal F_x$ the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. (3) $\mathcal F$ *has support proper over $S$* if $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is a closed subset of $X$ and this closed subset is proper over $S$ in the sense of (1).

proof.text: (Data: the scheme structure on $Z$.) For a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives the closed immersion $i_Z:Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z$ of sections vanishing at all points of $Z$, with $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $i_Z(Z_{\mathrm{red}})=Z$, and unique up to unique isomorphism over $X$ among reduced closed subschemes with underlying set $Z$. So the reduced induced structure of Stacks 01J4 is a well-defined object, and any two choices differ by an isomorphism $\varphi$ over $X$.

(Condition (1).) $Z$ is proper over $S$ iff the morphism $f\circ i_Z$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. This is condition (1) of Stacks Lemma 0CYL, which Definition 0CYM takes as the definition (the equivalence with conditions (2), (3) of 0CYL is the separate statement lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties (1), not used here). It does not depend on the choice in step 1: if $\varphi:Z'\to Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ is an isomorphism with $i_Z\varphi=i'$, then $f\circ i'=(f\circ i_Z)\circ\varphi$, and composing with an isomorphism preserves properness (isomorphisms are proper and proper morphisms are stable under composition, Mathlib IsProper instances; here only that $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of schemes over $S$, so separatedness, finite type and universal closedness transfer by definition). The hypothesis that $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] is not needed to state (1); Stacks imposes it because the equivalences of 0CYL fail without it.

source.place: Definition 0CYM, Lemma 0CYL (1), and the remark after 0CYM

proof.text: (Support.) For a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the underlying space of $X$ (the Zariski site), the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is the colimit of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module, so $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x:\mathcal F_x\neq0\}$ is a well-defined subset of $X$, as in Stacks Modules Definition 01AT. It need not be closed for an arbitrary $\mathcal F$; for $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent of finite type it is closed (Stacks 056J, the statement lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base (1)).

(Condition (3).) $\mathcal F$ has support proper over $S$ iff $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is closed and, as a closed subset, satisfies (1). Stacks speaks of 'the support of $\mathcal F$ is proper over $S$' only for finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$, where closedness holds automatically; requiring closedness in the definition extends the phrase to all $\mathcal O_X$-modules without changing it in the case Stacks considers.
